# TaskProfileV1

Source: [governed-intake-task-profile.v1.json](../contracts/governed-intake-task-profile.v1.json), schema `task-profile.v1`.
Source bytes: `sha256:ab05f35b94e44548dbfeff42820668bb1bea9816d5d7e23301e7e93a2644bacb`. This is a source digest, not a deployment receipt.

Provider/model/benchmark-independent semantic description of which kinds of reasoning determine whether one executable work unit succeeds. Triage describes the work; runtime owners interpret it.

TaskProfileV1 is semantic task truth, not execution policy. It never records or infers a model,
provider, account, pool, reasoning-effort setting, harness or benchmark. Design record and
acceptance: [spencer-shadley/code#6458](https://github.com/spencer-shadley/code/issues/6458).

## Placement in the triage lifecycle

Produced after scope-decomposition and before final-attributes, applying to: ordinary, atomic-high.
Produced by the triage agent in the same semantic pass; no extra model invocation, reviewer, panel or tournament.

Tracking parents: No aggregate profile; profile a distinct executable coordinator stage separately; never average, add or inherit child vectors.

## The five categories

| Category | Aliases | Question |
|---|---|---|
| `implement` | code, build, refactor, test, configure, migrate | How much of success is producing or modifying the actual artifact when the intended outcome/structure is substantially known? |
| `diagnose` | debug, investigate, research, RCA, localize | How much of success depends on discovering what is wrong/true and why from symptoms, evidence, experiments or system behavior? |
| `design` | architect, API, schema, protocol, algorithm | How much of success depends on choosing the technical structure of a future solution among meaningful alternatives? |
| `review` | review, audit, critique, verify, inspect | How much of success depends on evaluating an existing artifact/decision against requirements, invariants or quality expectations and identifying flaws? |
| `judgment` | decide, prioritize, compare, trade off, synthesize | How much of success depends on resolving ambiguous tradeoffs or making a semantic decision across multiple reasonable possibilities where there is no single mechanical answer? |

## Scoring

Spend 10 points on the kinds of reasoning that determine whether this task succeeds.

Exactly 10 integer points total, each category from 0 to 10.

Not meaning: lines of code, files touched, number of subtasks, wall-clock time, expected token count, issue description length, percentage of implementation steps, provider/model difficulty, priority, blast radius.

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 0 | not material |
| 1 | incidental |
| 2 | supporting |
| 3 | substantial secondary |
| 4 | major (tag threshold) |
| 5 | co-dominant |
| 10 | pure |
| 6-7 | dominant |
| 8-9 | strongly dominant |

## Confidence

| Level | Definition |
|---|---|
| high | Another competent profiler would probably produce the same dominant allocation with only one-point movement. |
| medium | Dominant shape is clear; a credible alternate reading could move about two points. |
| low | Ambiguous enough to change the dominant category or move three or more points; record the best vector; not a blocker. |

No `task-profile:high|medium|low` GitHub label exists in V1; confidence stays in the structured profile/receipt.

## Label projection

Apply a category label when its score is ≥ 4; otherwise apply exactly `task:mixed` and no category label.
At most 2 category labels result from one valid vector, by construction of a 10-point budget.
Labels are a derived browsing/search projection, never the runtime routing input; runtime consumes the full structured vector.

| Category | Label |
|---|---|
| `implement` | `task:implement` |
| `diagnose` | `task:diagnose` |
| `design` | `task:design` |
| `review` | `task:review` |
| `judgment` | `task:judgment` |

## Reuse and invalidation

Reconsider triggers: `acceptance-criteria-changed`, `issue-substantively-rewritten`, `decomposition-changed-executable-unit`, `investigation-revealed-different-reasoning-shape`, `current-value-or-supersession-changed-remaining-work`.

Never triggers reconsideration: `model-released`, `benchmark-rankings-changed`, `provider-credits-changed`, `machine-or-harness-availability-changed`, `bot-or-comment-updated-at`, `unrelated-branch-commits`, `profiler-preference`.

## Legacy fallback

Runtime fallback kind: `legacy-unprofiled`. Opportunistic acquisition during semantic triage only; no bulk backfill; runtime records an explicit fallback and never fabricates or persists a vector; absence never manufactures human-required.

## API integration and trust boundary

- `bindTaskProfileContract` derives a deterministic canonical-JSON identity; a checklist/rubric revision bump is never required for a TaskProfile-only source change.
- `validateTaskProfile` rejects any model/provider/account/pool/effort/harness/benchmark field; it accepts only the five-category vector, confidence and rationale.
- `deriveTaskLabels` and `evaluateTaskLabelProjection` are pure projections; labels never replace the full vector as runtime input.
- `decideTaskProfileReuse` reconsiders only on a listed trigger, a work-unit/scope-fingerprint mismatch or a contract-identity change; listed non-triggers (model release, benchmark movement, provider credits, harness/machine availability, comment churn, unrelated commits, profiler preference) never invalidate a valid record.
- `resolveRuntimeTaskProfile` never fabricates a vector: missing, invalid, stale or contract-mismatched evidence resolves to `legacy-unprofiled`, never `human-required` and never a blocking state.
- A tracking parent has no applicable aggregate profile; profile a distinct executable coordinator stage separately if one exists.
